methods.name: Revenue
methods.interpretation: Sales value under the simple price-volume assumption.

methods.name: Contribution per unit
methods.formula: selling price - variable cost per unit
methods.interpretation: Each unit contributes £20 to fixed costs and then profit.

methods.name: Total contribution
methods.interpretation: Total amount available to cover fixed costs before profit.

methods.name: Margin percentage
methods.worked_example: Net profit £30,000 ÷ revenue £200,000 × 100 = 15%. Contribution £80,000 ÷ revenue £200,000 × 100 = 40% contribution margin.
methods.interpretation: State the numerator explicitly because gross, operating, net-profit and contribution margins measure different things.

worked_examples: If net profit is £30,000 on £200,000 revenue, net profit margin is 15%.
If total contribution is £80,000 on £200,000 revenue, contribution margin is 40%.
interpretation: Contribution is not cash and not profit until fixed costs are considered.
Name the margin numerator and compare like-for-like definitions before interpreting differences.
common_errors: subtracting fixed cost to calculate contribution per unit
using the word margin without specifying whether it is gross, operating, net-profit or contribution margin
